issue.title: Edit and MultiEdit interEdit and MultiEdit interpret replacement text as JavaScript substitution patternspret replacement text as JavaScript substitution patterns

steps:
Create a file named split_lines.sh in the current directory with exactly the following content (keep every character as given):

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# split_lines.sh: print every field of the first argument on its own line
IFS=,
read -r -a parts <<< "$1"
for p in "${parts[@]}"; do
  echo "[$p]"
done
In split_lines.sh, change only the line `IFS=,` to `IFS=$'\n'` so the fields are split on newlines instead of commas. Do not change any other line.
expected: Edit（或 MultiEdit）应把 new_string 原样写入被替换处，即第 3 行变成 IFS=$'\n'、其余 6 行不变（依据：src/tools/fileEditTool.ts 的 Edit 描述 'Find a string in a file and replace it'、new_string = 'Replacement text'，multiEditTool.ts 同理，systemPrompt.ts:90 要求用 Edit 做精确修改）。
defect: 非 replace_all 的 Edit 走 String.prototype.replace(string, string)，new_string 里的 $' 被当作 JS 替换模式展开，落盘文件变成 'IFS=' + 原第 4 行起的整段内容 + 字面 \n'，行数从 7 增到 12、bash 报 unexpected EOF，而工具结果 completed 且 diff preview 显示的是请求的正确文本。

fault location.explanation: Contributing source location. See Root cause and the evidence review for observed behavior and limitations.

Root cause: The non-replace_all branch passes newString as a string argument to String.replace. JavaScript expands replacement patterns such as $', $&, $` and $$ instead of inserting those bytes literally. The archived Edit corrupts the script and the model later rewrites it. The final repaired file does not negate the intermediate tool failure.
